patients.label: adult intact male stray cat from Grao de Castellón, Spain, captured July 2023 for trap-neuter-release

identity_evidence.quote: The case was an adult (> 1 year old) intact male cat captured in July 2023 in the urban area of Grao de Castellón (39º 58′ 00′′ N, 10º 10′ 00′′ W, Castellon de la Plana, province of Spain) within the framework of a trap, neuter and release sterilization program run locally to control stray cat populations.

two female filarial nematodes with spontaneous movement were removed from the internal part of the spermatic cord from asymptomatic stray cat in Spain (Grao de Castellón, Castellon de la Plana, province of Spain).

attribution_limitations: Discussion segments b00067 and b00068 mix case-specific laboratory findings with general literature statements about feline subcutaneous dirofilariosis; attribution limited to the portions explicitly referring to 'our case' and 'the present report'

evidence.quote: Presence of the filarial nematodes in the internal part of the spermatic cord (arrows)
During the surgical procedure, two female filarial nematodes with spontaneous movement were removed from the internal part of the spermatic cord (Fig. 1).
a). Positive MCT with presence of multiple microfilariae (4x)
The presence of microfilariae was detected by using three methods (Fig. 2a and b).
b). Knott’s test revealed the presence of microfilariae of D. repens with the following morphological features: unsheathed with conical cephalic end and the tail like an umbrella’s handle (10x)

The modified Knott’s test revealed the presence of microfilariae of D. repens with the following morphological features: unsheathed with conical cephalic end and the tail like an umbrella’s handle (Fig. 2b).
c). Uterus with microfilaria from adult nematode (100x)
paired uteri containing morulae and microfilariae (Fig. 2c and d).
d) Cuticular surface with longitudinal ridge from adult nematode (200x)
the two adult females were composed of a thick cuticle with spaced longitudinal ridges on the surface
a). D. repens microfilariae with the presence of a pair of nuclei in the cephalic space (arrow) (Diff Quick, bar = 200 μm)
In our case, cephalic space of the microfilariae was compatible with D. repens because a pair of nuclei was present and separated from the rest of the somatic nuclei of the microfilariae (Fig. 3a)
b). D. immitis microfilarie from a canine clinical case with the absence of a pair of nuclei in the cephalic space (arrow) (Diff Quick, bar = 200 μm)

limitations: Literature review case counts and epidemiological summaries are background and not treated as original individually described patients; Fig3 panel b depicts a canine comparator case, not the index cat

review_method: Agent checked original case count, identity and species against source; roster scaffold from prior pilot; not physician adjudication.
